metadata.title: How teacher collaboration profiles connect to literacy instructional practices: evidence from PISA 2018 outcomes for Korea

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses secondary PISA 2018 Teacher Questionnaire data for Korean middle school literacy teachers (n=1,266) and estimates latent profiles and profile differences using MPlus 8.3. The manuscript does not report the use of PISA complex survey weights (e.g., student/teacher sampling weights) or any replicate-weight scheme, so it is unclear whether population-representative weighting was applied in the LPA/BCH estimation. Because the analysis is based on teacher questionnaire Likert-scale items and uses LPA with BCH auxiliary outcomes, the authors’ weighting approach (if any) is not documented. The main preprocessing described is handling missingness via FIML under a missing-at-random assumption; no additional outlier trimming or grade/school filtering is reported beyond the middle-school literacy teacher sample.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not model cognitive achievement outcomes from PISA; instead, it models teacher collaboration and five instructional-practice Likert constructs from the PISA 2018 Teacher Questionnaire. Since Plausible Values are generated for cognitive achievement domains (not for these non-cognitive questionnaire constructs), PV handling is not applicable. For missing data, the authors report full-information-maximum-likelihood (FIML) under missing-at-random; this is treated as a form of model-based missing-data handling rather than a PV-combining procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample consists of 1,266 full-time Korean middle school literacy teachers from the PISA 2018 Teacher Questionnaire. The study uses only the teacher questionnaire constructs: Korean literacy teacher collaboration (7 items) and five instructional practices (initiation of reading strategies, stimulation of reading engagement, direct instruction, adaptive instruction, feedback provision) as distal outcomes. No additional grade-band, school-type, or teacher-subject filtering is described beyond the middle school literacy teacher population; the questionnaire items are administered as 4-point Likert responses. Missing responses are handled using FIML under a missing-at-random assumption.

Using latent profile analysis (LPA) in MPlus 8.3, the authors tested 2–5 profile solutions and selected a four-profile model based on fit indices (AIC/BIC/SABIC), likelihood ratio tests (BLRT significant), and high classification quality (entropy reported around .961 for the four-profile solution). They then applied the BCH method to test differences in five instructional practices (direct instruction, adaptive instruction, initiation of reading strategies, stimulation of reading engagement, feedback provision) across the four collaboration profiles. The results show that teachers in the High Collaboration profile reported higher use of all five practices than other profiles, while the Assessment-centered Collaboration profile differed from Low Collaboration mainly in assessment-related instructional patterns. data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2018 Teacher Questionnaire data for Korean middle school literacy teachers (n=1,266) to identify latent profiles of teacher collaboration and to compare instructional-practice use across profiles. Using latent profile analysis (LPA) in MPlus 8.3, the authors tested 2–5 profile solutions and selected a four-profile model based on fit indices (AIC/BIC/SABIC), likelihood ratio tests (BLRT significant), and high classification quality (entropy reported around .961 for the four-profile solution). They then applied the BCH method to test differences in five instructional practices (direct instruction, adaptive instruction, initiation of reading strategies, stimulation of reading engagement, feedback provision) across the four collaboration profiles. The results show that teachers in the High Collaboration profile reported higher use of all five practices than other profiles, while the Assessment-centered Collaboration profile differed from Low Collaboration mainly in assessment-related instructional patterns. The study is correlational (no regression-based causal identification) and relies on self-report questionnaire measures; it also does not document the use of PISA complex survey weights.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is not an empirical machine-learning prediction/classification study; it uses latent profile analysis (a psychometric mixture-modeling approach) to discover collaboration subgroups and then compares instructional-practice means using BCH. Therefore, there are no ML algorithms to extract (ml_techniques is empty) and no predictive performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/RMSE/AUC) are applicable. The main results are profile structure and group differences rather than supervised ML model performance.
